source_name: Diebold Nixdorf corporate newsroom / investor news (incl. StockTitan mirror)
why_relevant: One of the two global ATM/branch-automation OEMs whose newsroom publishes named bank wins (observed pattern: 'X goes live with Diebold Nixdorf branch automation solutions'). Any Montenegrin bank fleet deal would most plausibly appear here or via its regional distributor.

source_name: NCR Atleos — corporate news and partner announcements
why_relevant: Post-2023 NCR spin-off focused on ATM hardware, software and ATM-as-a-Service; publishes partnership announcements naming banks and processors (observed: Mastercard/NCR Atleos/ITCARD). Primary candidate supplier for any Montenegrin ATM estate refresh.

Local business portal carrying company news, investment items and tenders. Vendors routinely place win announcements here in Montenegrin, making it the local-language mirror of supplier press releases and a bridge between vendor claims and tender/award records.

source_name: Banca d'Italia / CBCG instant-payments (TIPS Clone) supplier disclosure chain
why_relevant: Supplier-side identification of national payment infrastructure: reporting states the Bank of Italy is the technical provider of the TIPS Clone platform for Montenegro's instant-payments system (contract signed; go-live planned 20 July 2026). Shows the 'who supplies the rail' question is answerable from provider-side statements even for central-bank projects; anchor for tracking downstream bank/PSP integration vendors.

Dedicated regulator fintech portal (innovation hub / sandbox-style engagement). Expected to name fintech applicants, PSP innovators and partner projects, and to carry the National Fintech Strategy 2025-2029 workstreams — a pointer to future licensed payments buyers before they appear in the registers.

source_name: CBCG blog — 'Pregled FinTech ekosistema u Crnoj Gori' (fintech ecosystem mapping)
why_relevant: Regulator's own mapping exercise covering banks, MFIs, payment institutions and e-money institutions — a ready-made actor inventory and terminology source for the payments landscape, published by the body that licenses it.

source_name: Euronet ATMs Montenegro (euronetatms.me) — independent ATM deployer
why_relevant: Euronet operates as an Independent ATM Deployer in Montenegro with a local-language site (products include mobile ATMs and cash-deposit ATMs). IADs are first-class procurement actors: they buy ATM hardware, cash management, CIT, monitoring and switching independently of banks, and they sign branding/partnership deals with local banks.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (incl. Fintech Committee)
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 Montenegrin tech firms with an explicit Fintech Committee working with CBCG on the National Fintech Strategy. Its member list names local payments-adjacent suppliers and partners (observed mentions: Financial Solutions, POS4.me, Payten, Euro-Unit Montenegro, Coinis, Logate, Amplitudo, Bild Studio). Primary snowball engine for the local supplier/partner side of the payments ecosystem.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — Montenegrin Banking Association
why_relevant: All 11 member banks; runs a Payment Operations Committee and a Commission for Prevention of Payment Card Abuse, and comments on payments legislation. Industry-level coordination bodies are where shared infrastructure decisions (card scheme rules, interchange, fraud tooling, SEPA/instant migration) are pre-negotiated before any tender appears.

source_name: Western Union Montenegro — agent network page
why_relevant: Reveals the remittance distribution partnership map in Montenegro. Search results named the agent set as Pošta Crne Gore plus banks (Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Komercijalna, Lovćen, Podgorička, Prva, UCB, Ziraat), mobile operator MTEL and bus stations, with the WU principal role held since 2015 by payment institution Montenegro Transfers doo. Agent-network changes are partner-selection events for this cell.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — POS terminals / merchant acquiring pages
why_relevant: Montenegrin bank acquirer product page: terminal types, accepted schemes and wallet support disclose the underlying terminal vendor and processing capability set. Product-page change detection across ME acquirers is a cheap proxy for terminal-fleet refresh and gateway upgrades, which precede supplier selection.

source_name: Fiskalizacija.me / eFiskal.me — Montenegrin e-fiscalisation vendor ecosystem
why_relevant: E-fiscalisation is the adjacent mandate that drives merchant terminal replacement in Montenegro: every VAT taxpayer must report invoices electronically, certificates are issued by authorised bodies (Pošta Crne Gore and CoreIT were named), and vendors bundle fiscal software with POS hardware (e.g. Adeo POS, sekas.me, VG eFiskal). This maps the merchant-side buyer channel that competes with and complements bank acquiring.

source_name: European Payments Council — Montenegro SEPA accession coverage
why_relevant: Authoritative account of Montenegro's SEPA entry and the sector-wide go-live schedule. SEPA and TIPS-clone migration is the single largest forcing function for PSP and bank technology procurement in this market, so it dates the demand wave this cell tracks.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA (TIPS Clone) Project
why_relevant: An IFI-financed project (reported as a EUR 8m loan for payments-infrastructure modernisation) means World Bank procurement rules apply: procurement plans, general procurement notices and contract awards become publicly documented — a rare structured window into upcoming Montenegrin payments-infrastructure contracts.
